all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] core.hooksPath now names a user-level dir shared by every repository on the same content id, so tools installing into the resolved hooks dir write repo-specific hooks into the shared dir, and migration re-points away from and RemoveAlls the per-checkout dir together with any extra hooks placed there. A hand-added or tool-installed hook in one repo runs in every other gated repo on that id; on migration, extra hooks kept in <checkout>/.metareview/git-hooks are deleted and silently stop running.

[ADVISORY] isPreviousHookDir claims a content-addressed hook dir only directly under the CURRENT hooksHome(), so an install made under one XDG_DATA_HOME is classified as a foreign core.hooksPath when setup runs under a different or unset XDG_DATA_HOME, while the shell hooks match any */metareview/git-hooks/*. After an upgrade setup --install-hooks refuses metareview's own hooks as a conflict needing --force, uninstall says not metareview's, and the session-start check disagrees.

[ADVISORY] INSTALL.md still calls the materialized scripts per-clone scripts kept out of commits by the .gitignore block, and the hooksCurrent/PlanHookInstall/HookInstallPlan.Target comments in internal/setup/hooks.go describe the old per-checkout location. Readers look for or hand-repair the wrong directory.

[BUG] The recorded metareview.hooksId is trusted without checking it belongs to this repository, so a checkout copied with cp -r/rsync/backup restore (which carries .git/config) resolves the same hook dir as the original and both report correctly installed. Uninstalling in one copy removes pre-push/post-commit from the shared dir, silently ungating the other; a hook added in one copy runs in the other.

[BUG] When no hooksId is recorded, repoHooksID derives the id from sha256(commonDir) without checking the derived dir, and ApplyHookInstall overwrites .metareview-owner, so a repository created at the old path of a moved repository derives the moved one's id, installs into its live dir and takes over as owner. Uninstalling the new repository deletes the moved repository's live hook scripts, silently ungating it (mv repo repo.bak && git clone ... repo).

[BUG] A derived id never adopts an existing dir and nothing reclaims a dir whose owner file names this same path, so each rm -rf + re-clone + install at one path leaves a dir behind for good and after 64 cycles repoHooksID fails permanently (uninstall errors too). Scripted or agent re-clones to a fixed path leak dirs and then cannot install or uninstall the gate.

[ADVISORY] Uninstall keeps a user-added hook in the dir; the next install sees the derived dir exists and moves to another id, stranding the user's hook. After uninstall + reinstall the user's commit-msg silently no longer runs.

[BUG] orphaned() treats a dir as free when its owner path exists but that repo's config does not record the id; after mv repo repo.bak && git clone ... repo the owner path is the new clone, so it adopts the dir repo.bak still runs from, and ARCHITECTURE.md claims this sequence is protected. repo.bak's hooks run in the new clone; uninstalling the new clone deletes pre-push/post-commit from the shared dir, silently ungating repo.bak.

[BUG] releaseHookDir (uninstall and migration) deletes metareview's scripts whenever ownedBy holds, and ownedBy is true for every live repository carrying the same hooksId once the recorded owner path is gone, or for a copy at the owner path, so one of two live repositories sharing a dir can empty it under the other (cp -r a b; mv a c; uninstall in b; or tar a; mv a b; untar a; uninstall in a). A copy or restored backup deletes the gate scripts the moved original runs from; its pushes are no longer gated (setup --check there does report not installed).

[BUG] releaseHookDir removes any <x>/.metareview/git-hooks matched by shape, but the pre-#173 layout set an absolute core.hooksPath into the checkout, so a cp -r copy or restored backup still points at the original checkout's dir and install/uninstall run from the copy delete the original's scripts. The original's core.hooksPath still names the deleted dir, so git runs no pre-push there and its pushes go ungated until someone runs setup --check or reinstalls; a regression from main.

fix@0.summary: Per-repository user-level hook dir keyed by metareview.hooksId; shape-based ownership; migration refuses to drop other hooks; stale docs fixed.

fix@1.summary: Owner file per hook dir; copies derive their own id; only the owner releases a dir.

fix@2.summary: Derived hook ids skip existing dirs; bounded search.

fix@3.summary: Derived ids reuse orphaned dirs (owner gone or no longer records the id); live-recorded dirs never adopted.

fix@4.summary: Derived ids reuse only released dirs (no metareview scripts left); a dir holding the gate is never adopted.

fix@5.summary: Only per-checkout hook dirs are ever emptied; uninstall keeps the user-level dir and id.

fix@6.summary: Release a per-checkout hook dir only when its checkout is this repository's.
